title: Asymmetric information scrambling and eigenstate thermalization in inhomogeneous XXZ spin chains
abstract: Deterministic spatial inhomogeneity has become increasingly relevant in experimentally engineered quantum many-body systems, where interaction gradients can strongly influence nonequilibrium dynamics. Motivated by this, we investigate out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) and their connection to the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) in inhomogeneous XXZ spin chains. Using a deterministic spatially varying interaction profile, we show that finite interaction gradients ($δ>0$) induce a pronounced left--right asymmetry in information scrambling, as quantified by OTOCs. This asymmetry persists even when the system exhibits spectral signatures of quantum chaos, with operators on the strongly interacting side exhibiting suppressed scrambling. To elucidate the origin of the asymmetric finite-size long-time saturation value of OTOCs, we employ two complementary approaches. First, we analyze the diagonal matrix elements of the OTOC observables in the energy eigenbasis within the ETH framework. Second, we derive an analytical expression for the finite-size saturation value based on the overlap between the Hamiltonian and the OTOC observables, which explicitly incorporates the spatial interaction profile. The analytical prediction is fully consistent with the numerical results and provides a microscopic explanation for how deterministic interaction gradients generate the observed asymmetry in the long-time saturation of OTOCs.
summary: The paper analyzes how spatial variations in interactions within an XXZ spin chain lead to asymmetric information scrambling, quantified using OTOCs. By combining ETH theory with numerical calculations, the authors show that gradients suppress scrambling on strongly coupled sides and provide an analytical explanation for this asymmetry. This establishes deterministic inhomogeneity as a powerful tool for controlling quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates how deterministic spatial inhomogeneity affects information scrambling dynamics and eigenstate thermalization within quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The interaction gradient induces a pronounced left–right asymmetry in information scrambling, causing operators on strongly interacting sides to exhibit suppressed scrambling compared to weakly interacting sides.
method: The authors use Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs) and analyze diagonal matrix elements within the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH) framework.
model_or_system: The primary model is an inhomogeneous XXZ spin chain, characterized by a spatially varying interaction profile $Jz(i; \delta)$. The analysis also touches upon the inhomogeneous transverse-field Ising model (ITFIM).
key_observables: Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs), spectral statistics ($\langle r angle$), and diagonal matrix elements of local operators.
important_parameters: The interaction gradient strength $\delta$ is the key parameter, controlling the crossover from integrable ($\delta=0$) to chaotic regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the infinite-temperature regime and utilizes the ETH framework to connect dynamics to energy eigenbasis properties.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of spectral statistics ($\langle r angle$ vs. $\delta$), showing crossovers between Poisson, GOE, and nonergodic regimes; they also show OTOC dynamics revealing left-right asymmetry in scrambling.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes how spatial inhomogeneity modifies information scrambling by calculating OTOCs and applying ETH diagnostics to determine the finite-size saturation value of these correlators.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, microscopic mechanism—deterministic gradients—to control quantum information dynamics (scrambling) in lattice models, which is highly relevant for understanding engineered quantum simulators.
